counterfactual_missing_items: No verbatim span explicitly states 'post-infectious' or 'organizing pneumonia' as the final diagnosis; it is inferred from biopsy pattern and chronology.
No raw span documents resolution of the new left-upper-zone infiltrates after continued corticosteroid therapy.
No raw span explicitly excludes drug-induced organizing pneumonia from tacrolimus or mycophenolate.
decisive_items: He was treated with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and a prednisone taper, with clinical and radiographic resolution of infiltrates after 2 weeks.

Three weeks into therapy, he was asymptomatic except for an occasional dry cough. TMP-SMX was discontinued, and prednisolone was maintained at 10 mg daily. Laboratory studies then showed leukopenia (TLC 1400/μL; ANC 1050/μL). Chest radiograph revealed new left upper-zone infiltrates.

Transbronchial lung biopsy from the left upper lobe showed alveoli filled with inflammatory debris consisting of granulation tissue, interstitial inflammation, and areas of intra-alveolar fibrin deposition
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete: it combines the biopsy-proven organizing pneumonia pattern with the raw temporal sequence of treated Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, initial resolution, then new infiltrates and negative repeat BAL, supporting post-infectious organizing pneumonia. R7 has the same biopsy identity but lacks the post-infectious cause/time axis. R5 reflects the initial infection rather than the current process; R2 misinterprets the biopsy as bronchiolitis obliterans; R4 and R6 have no raw support beyond drug exposure; R3 is unrelated renal history.

rejected.why: No raw support span; only tacrolimus exposure, and the biopsy shows organizing pneumonia without drug-specific features.
Only mycophenolate exposure is cited; no raw evidence links it to pulmonary toxicity, and organizing pneumonia is nonspecific.
Biopsy shows organizing pneumonia, not constrictive bronchiolitis; BOS requires lung transplant context and airflow obstruction, both absent.
IgA nephropathy is the remote renal diagnosis and does not explain the current pulmonary infiltrates or biopsy findings.
Initial PJP was confirmed and treated, but repeat BAL was negative and the new infiltrates with organizing pneumonia biopsy indicate a post-infectious process, not active PJP.
